title: Genetic panel for inherited bowel cancer
what: This blood or saliva test checks several genes at once. Changes in them can run in families and raise the risk of bowel cancer.
why: If several relatives had bowel, uterine, or stomach cancer, or someone got it young, or if you have many polyps in your bowel.
duration: the blood draw usually takes 5 minutes; results usually come in 2 to 4 weeks
tell_doctor: Who in your family had bowel, uterine, stomach, or ovarian cancer, and at what age
How many polyps were found on your colonoscopies
If a relative already had a gene change found. Bring the report
If you had a blood transfusion or a bone marrow transplant

prepare.title: Counseling
prepare.text: It is best to talk with a geneticist before the test: which genes will be checked and what the result means.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You usually do not need to fast. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: Documents
prepare.text: Gather your colonoscopy and biopsy reports, if you have them.

bring: The list of relatives with cancer
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
Blood is taken from a vein into a tube
Sometimes saliva is collected instead of blood
The sample is sent to a genetics lab
feel: A quick prick, like a normal blood test
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse, and they will help you lie down
after: Results usually come in 2 to 4 weeks
Go over the result with a geneticist
If a change is found, colonoscopy is usually done earlier and more often. Your doctor will give you a schedule
Relatives may be offered a test for the same gene

faq.q: Why do this test if I already have colonoscopies?
faq.a: The result shows how often you need a colonoscopy and what other organs to check. It also helps your relatives.

faq.q: What does variant of uncertain significance mean?
faq.a: A change was found, but it is not yet known if it is harmful. Decisions are usually not based on it. The doctor watches for new findings.

reminders.text: Genetic test tomorrow. Bring the list of relatives with cancer and your colonoscopy reports.
